A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MicroG-4M and MicroG-Bench. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, including readable tables and rendered figures matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original HAR, captioning, VQA, and cross-domain transfer experiments in Tables 1–5, with qualitative and per-class results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds Gemini 2.5 Pro evaluations, additional HAR configurations, qualitative examples, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The dataset construction, action taxonomy, annotation workflow, and benchmark approach remain. Expanded descriptions and prompt templates document the existing annotation process without establishing a changed underlying method. Gemini 2.5 Pro is an added baseline.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three MicroG-4M tasks using 4,759 clips, 50 action classes, 1,238 captions, and 7,428 QA pairs, alongside the existing AVA/JHMDB transfer comparison. Additional models and dataset illustrations do not establish expanded task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds Gemini 2.5 Pro to captioning and VQA comparisons in Tables 4–5 and to HAR in new Table 11. Previous comparator identities remain; additional Slow and SlowFast temporal configurations extend settings rather than introduce new comparator methods.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds four temporal configurations. New experiments introduce three-frame Gemini captioning/VQA, highlighted-person HAR clips with binary indicators used as ranking scores, and warm-start timing measurements. Section 3 revises uniform 480p preprocessing to 480p or the highest available lower resolution. Section 5.1/Table 6 revise reported records from 13,251 to 13,261 while retaining video counts and split proportions; these disclosures do not establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: v4 Figure 5 retains v3 Figure 4 and adds six HAR cases examining posture and object-interaction errors. New Table 12 compares latency and memory for three video-language models. Existing captioning/VQA case studies remain, while enlargement of retained per-class plots is primarily a presentation change.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added median latency measurements are efficiency summaries, without an accompanying uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds four zero-shot HAR rows, Gemini results across three tasks, computational measurements, and qualitative predictions. Examples include Gemini VQA S-VQA 44.75 and binary-score HAR mAP 14.07%, under its stated settings. Most retained scores are identical; Table 1 changes SlowFast 4×16 test mAP from 42.10 to 42.09. Section 4 also changes Object Manipulation annotations from 4,976 to 4,986, matching the count already present in v3 Table 7.

T1.justification: Neither version presents substantive theoretical results or proofs. The added binary-vector encoding and metric computation describe an empirical evaluation procedure rather than a new mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The first-benchmark claim, three-task scope, and claimed difficulty of microgravity for terrestrial models remain. The rewritten contribution paragraph foregrounds standardized evaluation and characteristic failures already discussed in v3; the conclusion retains its scientific claims.

C2.justification: Appendices E.1 and G.3 expand explanations involving posture, brief contact, low visual salience, and backbone biases. Section 5.4 attributes Gemini's lexical/semantic score divergence partly to verbose answers. Appendix G.5 discusses overprediction and qualifies binary-score ranking metrics. The existing technical limitations remain under a renumbered appendix.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: Section 3 details annotation resources and verification; Appendix I supplies caption-refinement, QA-generation, and filtering prompts with four-keyframe inputs; Appendix G.5.1 explains Gemini HAR input preparation and output parsing. Hardware and numerical precision are newly reported. The new Ethics Statement specifies annotation/metadata-only distribution and independent video acquisition, although the abstract retains its broad availability statement.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Gemini 2.5, EgoCross, embodied one-shot video recognition, and referring atomic video action recognition, and removes the earlier Gemini-family and video-diffusion-survey references. The central positioning around the missing microgravity benchmark remains. Qwen bibliographic changes identify the same technical report.

P1.justification: Rewrites concentrate on the contribution paragraph, annotation explanation, and HAR interpretation. v4 adds an Ethics Statement, an LLM-use appendix, and supplementary subsections, and updates authors, affiliations, and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and much of the original prose remain.

P2.justification: v4 reorganizes the dense per-class figures into Figures 8–15 with enlarged plots, standardized axes, and explicit configurations. It adds a collection-pipeline diagram, expands the HAR qualitative figure, introduces annotation examples and a frame gallery, enlarges Table 2, and adds Tables 11–12. This substantially changes visual organization, including redisplay of retained evidence.

improvement.justification: Explicit annotation prompts, implementation details, clearer per-class displays, and additional baseline and efficiency evidence improve usability and empirical support. The gains are bounded: central findings remain stable, Gemini's binary ranking scores limit comparability, and the detailed LLM-generation account still conflicts with Appendix D's retained grammar-only claim. The metadata-only release statement also remains unreconciled with the abstract's broader availability claim.
